title.official: Political Declaration on Responsible Military Use of Artificial Intelligence and Autonomy
title.short: U.S.-led Political Declaration on military AI

issuer.name: United States of America (initiative); endorsing States

relevance.reason: The principal political declaration on responsible military use of AI and autonomy. It sets out non-legally binding measures for States across the lifecycle of military AI capabilities, including human command and control and compliance with international humanitarian law. It is not a treaty.
ai_provisions: Whole declaration — ten measures on responsible development, deployment and use of military AI and autonomy
relevance.excluded_scope: Non-binding political declaration; no verification, enforcement or legal obligation; not all States endorse it.

dates.notes: Launched at the REAIM Summit in The Hague on 16 February 2023. A revised text was published on 9 November 2023.

status_note: Open for endorsement by States; 58 endorsing States as of December 2024 according to Japan's Ministry of Defense. Endorsement is political, not a signature or ratification.

languages.note: English text is the initiative text; the U.S. State Department publishes translations. No authentic-language clause exists for a political declaration.

sources.note: Official page: launch at REAIM 2023, links to the declaration and translations, list of endorsing States as of 27 November 2024.
States that 58 States had endorsed the declaration as of December 2024 and that it is not legally binding.

rights.note: U.S. Government publication; generally not subject to U.S. copyright, but third-party content may be. Metadata only in this corpus.
